verdict.rationale: Stripe's embedded ACS mode is documented to run the full agent checkout lifecycle: cart and checkout, Stripe-created shared payment tokens routed to the seller, and order completion signalled by webhooks such as `checkout.session.completed`. Link CLI separately supplies human-approved one-time-use credentials for agent purchases. missing for 10: availability beyond private preview (gated by OCA agreements, limited to the US, Canada and select European countries, physical goods only), and independent or hands-on corroboration of a completed end-to-end agent purchase.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can complete a purchase end-to-end — checkout session, delegated payment credential, confirmed order

citations.quote: the full checkout lifecycle through Stripe, including product feed ingestion, cart management, fulfillment, and payment collection
Stripe handles routing, authentication, error retries, and shared payment token (SPT) creation so you don’t need to integrate directly with each seller.
ACS works across multiple commerce protocols, so your AI interface can discover products, collect payment information, and complete purchases on behalf of sellers.
Creates a spend request for a specific purchase. The customer approves it, and Link returns a one-time-use payment credential your agent uses to pay.
Stripe sends `checkout.session.completed` after the agent completes an order.
